questions: Did these symptoms begin suddenly, over hours to days?
Are the jerky movements present even when you are sitting still and relaxed, or only when you try to use your limbs?
Has anyone in your family had similar problems with movement or balance?
Do you drink alcohol heavily on most days?
Do you have any numbness or tingling in your legs or feet?
Have you noticed any double vision or other problems with your vision?
Do you have difficulty with your speech or with swallowing?
Have you been having problems with your memory or thinking clearly?
Did you have a recent infection or serious illness shortly before this started?
Are you currently taking any medications that affect the brain, such as for seizures, mood, or psychosis?
Have you had any episodes of urinary incontinence?
Have you ever been diagnosed with cancer?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Post-infectious opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome (Kinsbourne syndrome)

Alternatives:
1. Paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration with myoclonus (occult malignancy, e.g. small-cell lung or breast cancer) — anti-Ri, anti-Hu, anti-Yo, anti-amphiphysin antibodies not yet tested
2. Hashimoto's (steroid-responsive) encephalopathy — anti-TPO/anti-thyroglobulin antibodies and thyroid function not yet tested
3. Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (sCJD) — though MRI and preserved cognition make this unlikely; would need EEG and 14-3-3/real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) assay on CSF
